newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo plans diplomatic shakeup.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo plans diplomatic shakeup.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's Congo pledged on Friday to restructure its diplomatic service, pay off overdue salaries and weed out those who are not "real diplomats".
Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha said in the capital Kinshasa that many diplomats and their dependents would be repatriated soon. He gave no details.

"The government is seriously grappling with the question of salaries. We have to restructure the Congolese diplomatic service at all cost," he told reporters on Friday. "There are people who are there without being real diplomats."
Diplomats were long been neglected under ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko. Many have not been paid for at least three years.
Tales of the more impoverished members of the Zairean diplomatic corps made headlines. Others resorted to all kinds of business to make ends meet.

Kabila toppled Mobutu in May after a seven-month civil war. He proclaimed himself president with sweeping powers and banned political activity. He has pledged to bring order to the former Zaire that he has renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
